visual: SLIDE: Section Title: 'How It Was Made'. Accent glow.
caption: Section three: how Chhaya was built.

visual: SLIDE: DATA slide: The Datasets overview.
caption:
We evaluated on two open datasets
and one synthetic patient.

visual: SLIDE: Card 1: ShanghaiT2DM dataset details.
caption:
ShanghaiT2DM includes 100 Type 2 diabetes patients
across 109 recordings.

visual: SLIDE: Shanghai details: 15-min sensor, fingersticks, diet text, drugs.
caption:
It provides 15-minute sensor readings,
fingersticks, diet logs, and labs.

visual: SLIDE: Shanghai licence: CC BY 4.0.
caption: ShanghaiT2DM is open under CC BY 4.0.

visual: SLIDE: Card 2: CGMacros dataset details.
caption:
CGMacros includes 45 free-living participants
wearing dual sensors and Fitbit.

visual: SLIDE: CGMacros licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 non-commercial.
caption:
CGMacros is licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
for non-commercial research.

visual: SLIDE: Split by patient card: 'is_dev_patient()'.
caption:
Crucially, data is split strictly by patient,
never by row.

visual: SLIDE: Population priors on dev, evaluated on test once.
caption:
Priors are tuned on dev patients
and evaluated once on held-out test patients.

visual: SLIDE: Data hygiene: checksum verification.
caption:
All datasets are checksummed
and verified on download.

visual: SLIDE: BUILD slide: Step 1: Raw data to Recording schema.
caption:
The architecture follows a strict
one-way pipeline.

visual: SLIDE: BUILD step 2: Recording data class.
caption:
The Recording schema is the only data structure
that crosses module boundaries.

visual: SLIDE: BUILD step 3: build_inputs creates JAX arrays.
caption:
Module build_inputs converts recordings
into clean numerical arrays.

visual: SLIDE: BUILD step 4: fit_twin optimizes parameters.
caption:
Module fit_twin optimizes patient parameters
using JAX x64 acceleration.

visual: SLIDE: BUILD step 5: simulate_ensemble generates trajectories.
caption:
Module simulate_ensemble simulates ODE trajectories
and covariance envelopes.

visual: SLIDE: BUILD step 6: Precomputed JSON bundle to dashboard.
caption:
The build command writes precomputed JSON bundles
for the browser.

visual: SLIDE: Serverless static design: zero latency inference.
caption:
The browser app computes nothing live:
every curve is precomputed and verified.

visual: SLIDE: TWIN slide: Extended Discrete-Event Simulator (E-DES).
caption:
The physiological core is an E-DES model
implemented in JAX.

visual: SLIDE: ODE equations in 1-minute steps with RK4.
caption:
Ordinary differential equations step at one minute
using fourth-order Runge-Kutta.

visual: SLIDE: Two-compartment gut model details.
caption:
A two-compartment gut model simulates
carbohydrate digestion and appearance.

visual: SLIDE: JAX precision: x64 enabled.
caption:
We use 64-bit floating point precision
in JAX to prevent numerical underflow.

visual: SLIDE: Pure functional implementation.
caption:
Pure functional simulation ensures
exact reproducibility across platforms.

visual: SLIDE: 7 personal parameters card.
caption: The twin fits seven patient-specific parameters.

visual: SLIDE: Parameter 1: absorption rate k_abs.
caption:
Absorption rate k_abs governs gut emptying
and appearance into plasma.

visual: SLIDE: Parameter 2: basal glucose Gb.
caption:
Basal glucose Gb represents steady-state
hepatic glucose production.

visual: SLIDE: Parameter 3: beta responsiveness.
caption:
Beta-cell responsiveness captures
insulin secretion capacity.

visual: SLIDE: Parameter 4: dawn amplitude.
caption:
Dawn amplitude models early morning
circadian elevation in glucose.

visual: SLIDE: Parameter 5: exercise sensitivity.
caption:
Exercise sensitivity scales muscle glucose uptake
from physical activity.

visual: SLIDE: Parameter 6: meal-logging bias.
caption:
Meal-logging bias adjusts for patient
underreporting of carb grams.

visual: SLIDE: Parameter 7: insulin-mediated disposal fraction.
caption:
And insulin-mediated disposal fraction
balances clearance.

visual: SLIDE: MAP estimation and Laplace approximation.
caption:
We fit parameters with MAP estimation
and compute a Laplace uncertainty band.

visual: SLIDE: L-BFGS-B optimization speed.
caption:
The optimizer finds the posterior mode
using L-BFGS-B in seconds.

visual: SLIDE: Parameter covariance from Hessian matrix.
caption:
The Hessian at the mode gives the covariance
for realistic uncertainty bands.

visual: SLIDE: The Blend slide: 50% physiology + 50% average day.
caption:
The estimate is an equal blend of physiology
and the patient's average day.

visual: SLIDE: Why blend works: errors are only partly correlated.
caption:
Physiology captures today's meals,
while average day captures unlogged habits.

visual: SLIDE: Fingerstick assimilation filter.
caption:
A Kalman-style filter assimilates fingersticks
as sparse evidence.

visual: SLIDE: Updating baseline and drift states.
caption:
Each fingerstick updates both baseline glucose
and running drift.

visual: SLIDE: Non-negotiable rules card.
caption: We followed four non-negotiable rules.

visual: SLIDE: Rule 1: No data leakage. Timestamps strictly > split.
caption:
Rule one: no data leakage.
Scored timestamps strictly follow the split.

visual: SLIDE: Test assertions against sensor leakage.
caption:
Automated tests alter hidden sensor values
and assert features do not move.

visual: SLIDE: Rule 2: Bars written first in PREREGISTRATION.md.
caption:
Rule two: all pass bars were written
before test runs in PREREGISTRATION.md.

visual: SLIDE: Rule 3: Report what happened. Publish misses.
caption:
Rule three: report what happened.
A miss is published, never hidden.

visual: SLIDE: Rule 4: Plain baselines acknowledged.
caption:
Rule four: where a plain baseline wins,
we say so plainly.

visual: SLIDE: Test suite: 400+ automated pytest tests.
caption:
Over 400 automated tests enforce compliance
on every commit.

visual: SLIDE: Scientific integrity recap.
caption: Truth rules take precedence over marketing.

visual: SLIDE: Synthetic recovery verification.
caption:
Synthetic recordings verify that ground truth
parameters can be recovered.

visual: SLIDE: Unit test coverage summary.
caption: Comprehensive assertions on physiological bounds.

visual: SLIDE: LIMITS slide: What Chhaya Is Not.

visual: SLIDE: Limit 1: No Indian dataset.
caption:
First: there is no Indian patient dataset
in our evaluation.

visual: SLIDE: Limit 2: Supervised inpatient care.
caption:
Second: Shanghai data was inpatient care
with adjusted medication.

visual: SLIDE: Limit 3: Hidden windows at most 11 days.
caption:
Third: hidden windows are at most eleven days,
not giving a fixed expiry day.

visual: SLIDE: Observation on inpatient drift rate.
caption:
We observed about 1 mg/dL per day downward
drift in supervised inpatient care.

visual: SLIDE: Observation on free-living drift rate.
caption:
In free-living participants, no significant
drift was detected over a week.

visual: SLIDE: Case series of 8 re-recorded patients.
caption:
Eight patients were re-recorded up to 168 days
later as an observational case series.

visual: SLIDE: Limit 4: Physiology effect is ~2%.
caption:
Fourth: the physiological model effect
is approximately two per cent.

visual: SLIDE: Limit 5: No exogenous insulin kinetics in ODE.
caption:
Fifth: no exogenous insulin kinetics
or drug dynamics in the ODE.

visual: SLIDE: Clinical boundary card.
caption:
Chhaya is an investigative tool,
not an autonomous clinical decision system.

caption:
We display no meal alert
and no excursion probabilities.

visual: SLIDE: Miss consequence 2: Record shown as context, not gain.
caption:
The health record is presented as context,
not as predictive power.

visual: SLIDE: Miss consequence 3: Converted fingerstick average used.
caption:
Patient summary figures use the plain converted
fingerstick average.

visual: SLIDE: Miss consequence 4: Staleness prompt is descriptive only.
caption:
The staleness prompt is purely descriptive,
never clinical advice.

visual: SLIDE: Not for Type 1 diabetes or acute dosing.
caption:
Chhaya is not for acute hypoglycemia
or insulin dosing.
